punchline: Gabor Maté noticed that many people who could never say no had bodies that eventually did it for them.
thirty_sec: Physician Gabor Maté kept meeting the same kind of person among his chronically ill patients: always helping, never refusing, anger held in. He suggests that years of that kind of stress wear on the body, and the body ends up saying the no the person could not. He is clear this is about understanding, not blame, and the stress-disease link is still debated.
